name: Satyendra Nath Bose
known_for: Sent a paper to Einstein that changed quantum physics forever. The 'boson' — the particle that gives matter its mass — is named after him.

name: Hedy Lamarr
known_for: Hollywood star who co-invented frequency-hopping spread spectrum technology during WWII — a concept that underpins modern WiFi and Bluetooth.

name: Isaac Asimov
known_for: Biochemistry professor who became the most prolific science fiction writer in history, authoring over 500 books and dreaming up the Three Laws of Robotics.

name: Sergei Korolev
known_for: The secret mastermind behind the Soviet space program — Sputnik, Laika, Gagarin — whose identity was hidden from the world until after his death.

name: Isaac Newton
known_for: Invented calculus, discovered the laws of motion and universal gravitation, and split white light into a rainbow — all before turning 30. Spent his later years obsessed with alchemy and biblical prophecy.

name: Louis Braille
known_for: Blinded in an accident at age three, he invented the tactile reading system that bears his name — at just fifteen years old.

name: Georg Cantor
known_for: Proved that some infinities are bigger than others, a discovery so radical it drove him to breakdowns and earned savage attacks from fellow mathematicians.

name: Konrad Zuse
known_for: Built the world's first programmable computer (the Z3) in his parents' living room in Berlin in 1941, while Allied bombers flew overhead.

name: Stephen Hawking
known_for: Given two years to live at 21, he went on to rewrite our understanding of black holes and time, becoming the most recognizable scientist since Einstein.

name: Alfred Russel Wallace
known_for: Independently conceived the theory of natural selection while delirious with fever in Malaysia, then graciously shared credit with Darwin.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
known_for: Wrote 'The Second Sex,' the book that essentially invented modern feminist philosophy, arguing that 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.'

name: Donald Knuth
known_for: Wrote 'The Art of Computer Programming,' a multi-volume masterwork so exacting he invented an entire typesetting system (TeX) because he hated how his books looked in print.

name: Yellapragada SubbaRow
known_for: Discovered ATP's role in cellular energy, developed methotrexate for cancer, and synthesized folic acid — yet remains almost unknown because he was an immigrant who didn't self-promote.

name: Nikolai Pirogov
known_for: Pioneer of field surgery and the first to use ether anesthesia in a military operation. His anatomical atlas, based on frozen cadaver cross-sections, was decades ahead of its time.

name: Sydney Brenner
known_for: Chose the humble roundworm C. elegans as a model organism and used it to crack open the genetics of organ development, winning a Nobel at 75.

name: Albert Schweitzer
known_for: Theologian, organist, and philosopher who gave it all up to study medicine, then spent decades running a hospital in equatorial Africa.

name: Sofia Kovalevskaya
known_for: Entered a sham marriage just to leave Russia and study math. Became the first woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics and first to hold a full professorship in Europe.

name: Edward Teller
known_for: The 'father of the hydrogen bomb' — a brilliant, controversial physicist whose testimony helped destroy Oppenheimer's career.

name: Dian Fossey
known_for: Spent 18 years living among mountain gorillas in Rwanda, revolutionizing our understanding of great apes before being murdered in her cabin — a crime still unsolved.

name: Benjamin Franklin
known_for: Flew a kite into a thunderstorm to prove lightning is electrical, invented the lightning rod and bifocals, and helped found a nation — all without a formal education.

name: Daniel Hale Williams
known_for: Performed one of the first successful open-heart surgeries in 1893 and founded Provident Hospital, the first non-segregated hospital in America.

name: James Watt
known_for: Didn't invent the steam engine but improved it so dramatically that he powered the Industrial Revolution. The unit of power — the watt — keeps his name alive in every light bulb.

name: Andre Marie Ampere
known_for: Founded the science of electrodynamics and gave his name to the unit of electric current. Taught himself advanced math from library books as a teenager.

name: Camillo Golgi
known_for: Invented a staining technique in a hospital kitchen that made individual neurons visible for the first time, opening the entire field of modern neuroscience.

name: Ukichiro Nakaya
known_for: Japanese physicist who created the first artificial snowflakes and proved that every crystal's shape is a frozen diary of the atmospheric conditions it fell through.

name: Francis Bacon
known_for: The father of the scientific method, who argued knowledge should come from observation and experiment rather than ancient authority. Died after catching pneumonia while stuffing a chicken with snow.

name: Lev Landau
known_for: Soviet theoretical physicist who made foundational contributions to nearly every branch of physics. Kept a ranking of physicists where Einstein alone occupied the top tier.

name: David Hilbert
known_for: Posed 23 unsolved problems in 1900 that shaped 20th-century mathematics. When told a student had dropped math for poetry: 'Good — he did not have enough imagination for mathematics.'

name: Edith Clarke
known_for: First woman to earn an electrical engineering degree from MIT and first female professor of EE in the US. Invented a graphical calculator for solving power line problems.

name: Berta Karlik
known_for: First woman to be a full professor at the University of Vienna. Discovered that astatine occurs naturally, making it the last naturally occurring element to be found.

name: Robert Boyle
known_for: Often called the first modern chemist. His law relating pressure and volume of gases is still taught in every introductory science class.

name: Joseph-Louis Lagrange
known_for: Reformulated Newtonian mechanics into elegant mathematical poetry. Napoleon called him 'the lofty pyramid of the mathematical sciences.'

name: Paul Erdos
known_for: Homeless by choice, fueled by amphetamines and coffee, he wandered the world collaborating with so many mathematicians that your 'Erdos number' measures how far you are from his orbit.

name: Lewis Carroll
known_for: Oxford mathematician Charles Dodgson wrote 'Alice in Wonderland' partly as a satire of the bizarre new abstract mathematics emerging in his era.

name: Rosalyn Yalow
known_for: Co-developed radioimmunoassay, a technique so sensitive it could detect a teaspoon of sugar dissolved in a lake, revolutionizing endocrinology and winning her the Nobel Prize.

name: Abdus Salam
known_for: First Pakistani and first Muslim Nobel laureate in science. Unified electromagnetism and the weak nuclear force — yet was declared non-Muslim in his own country.

name: Robert Noyce
known_for: Co-invented the integrated circuit and co-founded Intel. Known as 'the Mayor of Silicon Valley,' he was the archetype of the charismatic tech founder.

name: Hideki Yukawa
known_for: First Japanese Nobel laureate. Predicted the existence of mesons — the particles that glue atomic nuclei together — purely from theoretical reasoning.

name: Har Gobind Khorana
known_for: Born in a tiny village in British India, he cracked the genetic code and synthesized the first artificial gene, winning the Nobel Prize in Physiology.

name: Erwin Schrodinger
known_for: His wave equation is the beating heart of quantum mechanics. Invented a thought experiment about a cat simultaneously alive and dead — and it still haunts physics.

name: Emilio Segre
known_for: Discovered the antiproton and technetium, the first artificially produced element. Fled Mussolini's Italy and joined the Manhattan Project.

name: Fritz Zwicky
known_for: Predicted dark matter, neutron stars, and gravitational lensing decades before anyone confirmed them. Colleagues found him insufferable; the universe proved him right.

name: Gaston Julia
known_for: Lost his nose in WWI and wore a leather strap across his face for life. His work on iterated functions gave rise to the mesmerizing Julia sets.

name: Clyde Tombaugh
known_for: A Kansas farm boy who built telescopes from old car parts and discovered Pluto at age 24. Some of his ashes rode aboard the New Horizons spacecraft to Pluto in 2015.

name: J.C. Bose
known_for: Indian polymath who pioneered wireless communication before Marconi, then stunned the world by demonstrating that plants respond to stimuli much like animals do.

name: Joseph Priestley
known_for: Discovered oxygen (he called it 'dephlogisticated air'), invented soda water, and was so politically radical that a mob burned his house down.

name: Godfrey Harold Hardy
known_for: Rescued Ramanujan from obscurity, championed pure mathematics as an art form, and wrote 'A Mathematician's Apology,' the most beautiful defense of useless knowledge ever penned.

name: Daniel Bernoulli
known_for: Explained why airplane wings generate lift and why shower curtains blow inward. His father Johann was so jealous of his success that he tried to steal credit for his work.

name: Dmitri Mendeleev
known_for: Arranged the elements into the periodic table — reportedly after seeing the pattern in a dream — and boldly predicted elements that hadn't been discovered yet.

name: John von Neumann
known_for: Perhaps the last true polymath — he invented game theory, designed the architecture of modern computers, and could multiply eight-digit numbers in his head as a child.

name: Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin
known_for: Discovered that stars are made primarily of hydrogen and helium. Her doctoral thesis was called 'the most brilliant ever written in astronomy,' yet her male advisor told her to retract her conclusion.

name: Thomas Edison
known_for: Holder of over a thousand patents including the phonograph and practical light bulb. His real genius was industrializing the process of invention itself.

name: Josiah Willard Gibbs
known_for: Founded chemical thermodynamics and statistical mechanics in papers so dense almost nobody read them. Einstein later called him 'the greatest mind in American history.'

name: Charles Darwin
known_for: Spent five years on the Beagle, twenty years agonizing over the implications, then published 'On the Origin of Species' and changed how we understand every living thing.

name: William Shockley
known_for: Co-invented the transistor, the tiny switch that made the digital age possible. His later embrace of eugenics remains a cautionary tale about genius and moral blindness.

name: Galileo Galilei
known_for: Pointed a telescope at the heavens and saw Jupiter's moons, lunar craters, and Venus's phases — evidence that shattered the geocentric universe and earned him house arrest for life.

name: Ernst Mach
known_for: His work on supersonic motion gave us the Mach number. His insistence that science stick to observable quantities directly influenced Einstein's relativity.

name: Alessandro Volta
known_for: Invented the first true battery — the voltaic pile — proving electricity could be generated chemically. Napoleon was so impressed he made Volta a count.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus
known_for: Moved the Earth. His heliocentric model, published as he lay dying, launched the scientific revolution by placing the Sun — not us — at the center.

name: Ludwig Boltzmann
known_for: Proved that the second law of thermodynamics is statistical, not absolute. His entropy formula S = k log W is carved on his tombstone. Took his own life, despairing that his ideas would never be accepted.

name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
known_for: The 'Prince of Mathematicians' — at three he corrected his father's arithmetic, at nineteen he proved the constructibility of the 17-gon, and he never really slowed down.

name: Heinrich Hertz
known_for: First to prove the existence of electromagnetic waves predicted by Maxwell. Died at 36, never imagining his discovery would spawn radio, TV, and wireless everything.

name: W.E.B. Du Bois
known_for: Pioneer of empirical sociology and data visualization. His hand-drawn charts for the 1900 Paris Exposition are still studied for their beauty and clarity.

name: George Herbert Mead
known_for: Founded symbolic interactionism, the idea that the self is constructed through social interaction. Never published a book — his students compiled his lectures after he died.

name: Linus Pauling
known_for: Only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes — one in Chemistry, one for Peace. Revolutionized our understanding of chemical bonds, then spent decades insisting vitamin C cured everything.

name: Alexander Graham Bell
known_for: Invented the telephone while trying to help deaf people communicate. His mother and wife were both deaf, and teaching the deaf remained his lifelong passion.

name: Miriam Menkin
known_for: Achieved the first in vitro fertilization of a human egg in 1944. Her work was largely forgotten because she was a lab technician, not a professor.

name: Georg Ohm
known_for: Discovered the fundamental law relating voltage, current, and resistance. His work was initially dismissed; he resigned his post in despair before finally receiving recognition.

name: Valentina Tereshkova
known_for: A textile worker and amateur parachutist who became the first woman in space in 1963. She orbited Earth 48 times — more than all American astronauts combined at that point.

name: Luther Burbank
known_for: The 'plant wizard' who developed over 800 varieties of plants, including the Russet Burbank potato — the one McDonald's still uses for french fries.

name: Otto Hahn
known_for: Discovered nuclear fission — then wept when he learned it had been used to build the atomic bomb.

name: Yuri Gagarin
known_for: First human in space. A bricklayer's son from rural Russia who orbited the Earth on April 12, 1961, and returned with the immortal words: 'The Earth is blue.'

name: Joseph Lister
known_for: Pioneer of antiseptic surgery. Before Lister, surgeons operated in street clothes and never washed their hands. His carbolic acid sprays saved countless lives.

name: Urbain Le Verrier
known_for: Discovered Neptune not by looking through a telescope, but by calculating where it had to be from perturbations in Uranus's orbit. Pure mathematics revealing an unseen world.

name: Gustav Kirchhoff
known_for: His circuit laws are still fundamental to electrical engineering, and he co-invented spectroscopy, letting us determine what distant stars are made of without visiting them.

name: Albert Einstein
known_for: In a single 'miracle year' he explained Brownian motion, the photoelectric effect, and special relativity. Then spent a decade inventing general relativity, reimagining gravity as the curvature of spacetime.

name: Sylvia Earle
known_for: Known as 'Her Deepness,' she set the solo depth record for untethered diving and has spent over 7,000 hours underwater championing ocean conservation.

name: Caroline Herschel
known_for: First woman to discover a comet (she found eight), first to be paid for scientific work by the British crown, and first to receive honorary membership in the Royal Astronomical Society.

name: Gottlieb Daimler
known_for: Built the first high-speed internal combustion engine and the first four-wheeled automobile, co-founding the company that became Mercedes-Benz.

name: Joseph Fourier
known_for: Discovered that any function can be decomposed into sine waves — powering everything from MP3s to medical imaging. Also the first person to study the greenhouse effect.

name: Katsuko Saruhashi
known_for: Japanese geochemist who tracked radioactive fallout from nuclear tests across the Pacific and proved it was contaminating marine life worldwide.

name: Emmy Noether
known_for: Her theorem connecting symmetry to conservation laws is one of the most beautiful results in all of physics. Einstein called her the most important woman in the history of mathematics.

name: Wernher von Braun
known_for: Designed the V-2 rocket for Nazi Germany, then the Saturn V that carried humans to the Moon — the most morally complicated journey in the history of engineering.

name: Pierre-Simon Laplace
known_for: The 'French Newton' who formulated celestial mechanics. When Napoleon asked why God didn't appear in his equations: 'I had no need of that hypothesis.'

name: Wilhelm Rontgen
known_for: Discovered X-rays by accident, then took the first medical X-ray — his wife's hand, bones and wedding ring glowing on the plate. She reportedly said: 'I have seen my death.'

name: Robert Bunsen
known_for: Famous for the Bunsen burner (which his assistant actually designed), his real breakthrough was co-inventing spectroscopy, revealing that every element has a unique fingerprint of light.

name: Rene Descartes
known_for: Invented coordinate geometry while lying in bed watching a fly on the ceiling. His 'I think, therefore I am' remains philosophy's most famous one-liner.

name: Sophie Germain
known_for: Taught herself math from her father's library, wrote to Gauss under a male pseudonym, and made major contributions to number theory and the physics of vibrating surfaces.

name: William Harvey
known_for: Demonstrated that the heart pumps blood through a closed circulatory system — overturning Galen's 1,400-year-old model and launching modern physiology.

name: Maria Sibylla Merian
known_for: At 52, sailed to Suriname to study insects — astonishing for any 17th-century European, let alone a woman. Her hand-painted illustrations of metamorphosis are masterpieces of both science and art.

name: Paul Cohen
known_for: Proved that the continuum hypothesis is independent of set theory — mathematics itself has limits we cannot escape. Won the Fields Medal for this unsettling result.

name: Jane Goodall
known_for: Went to Tanzania at 26 with no degree and discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools — overturning the definition of what makes us human.

name: Linus Torvalds
known_for: Created Linux as a hobby project at 21, then accidentally built the OS that runs most of the world's servers, phones, and supercomputers.

name: Fazlur Rahman Khan
known_for: The 'Einstein of structural engineering' who invented the tube structure design that made modern skyscrapers possible, including the Willis Tower.

name: Robert Oppenheimer
known_for: Led the Manhattan Project and quoted the Bhagavad Gita upon witnessing the first nuclear detonation: 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.'

name: James Watson
known_for: Co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA — though much of the crucial evidence came from Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography, for which she received too little credit.

name: Mary Jackson
known_for: NASA's first Black female engineer. She had to petition the city of Hampton for permission to attend the graduate courses required for her promotion — because the school was whites-only.

name: Percy Lavon Julian
known_for: Grandson of enslaved people who became a pioneering organic chemist. Synthesized physostigmine and cortisone from soybeans. His home was firebombed by racists — twice.

name: Christiaan Huygens
known_for: Invented the pendulum clock, discovered Saturn's rings and its moon Titan, and proposed the wave theory of light — the most versatile scientist between Galileo and Newton.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
known_for: Filled 7,000 notebook pages with flying machines, anatomical studies, and ideas centuries ahead of their time. The original Renaissance polymath.

name: Leonhard Euler
known_for: The most prolific mathematician ever — blind in one eye by 30, totally blind by 60, somehow more productive after losing his sight. His formula e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0 is the most beautiful equation.

name: Wilbur Wright
known_for: With his brother Orville, achieved the first powered heavier-than-air flight at Kitty Hawk. Neither had a college degree or any formal engineering training.

name: Max Weber
known_for: Founded modern sociology. His 'Protestant Ethic' linked Calvinist anxiety about salvation to the rise of capitalism — an argument scholars are still debating.

name: Rita Levi-Montalcini
known_for: Discovered nerve growth factor while running a secret lab in her bedroom during the Nazi occupation of Italy. Won the Nobel at 77 and lived to 103.

name: Max Planck
known_for: Reluctantly introduced the quantum — energy comes in discrete packets — because it was the only way to make his equations work. It shattered classical physics.

name: Annie Easley
known_for: One of NASA's first African American employees, she developed code for the Centaur rocket stage that launched communication satellites and planetary probes.

name: Wolfgang Pauli
known_for: Predicted the neutrino and discovered the exclusion principle. Famous for withering criticism — 'not even wrong' was his verdict on bad physics.

name: Charles Richter
known_for: Developed the Richter scale for measuring earthquake magnitude. Also a nudist and published poet — far more interesting than his famous scale suggests.

name: Frederick Banting
known_for: Co-discovered insulin and chose not to put his name on the patent, believing life-saving medicine should be available to everyone. Sold the patent for one dollar.

name: Samuel Morse
known_for: An accomplished painter who invented Morse code and the practical telegraph, sending the first message — 'What hath God wrought' — from Washington to Baltimore in 1844.

name: Kurt Godel
known_for: Proved that any consistent mathematical system must contain truths that cannot be proved within it — the most devastating result in the history of logic. Died of starvation, refusing to eat food not prepared by his wife.

name: Hertha Ayrton
known_for: Expert on the electric arc and sand ripple formation. First woman to read a paper at the Royal Society, though they refused to let her become a member.

name: Henri Poincare
known_for: The last mathematician who could work in every branch of the field. Discovered chaos theory a century before it had a name, and came tantalizingly close to special relativity before Einstein.

name: Claude Shannon
known_for: Invented information theory in a single paper, creating the foundation for all digital communication. Also built a flame-throwing trumpet and a machine whose sole purpose was to turn itself off.

name: Carl Linnaeus
known_for: Invented binomial nomenclature — the system that gives every species a two-part Latin name. Even taxonomists need a brand.

name: Santiago Ramon y Cajal
known_for: Father of modern neuroscience. His hand-drawn illustrations of neurons are both scientific landmarks and works of art, revealing the brain's architecture with breathtaking precision.

name: Benjamin Spock
known_for: His 'Baby and Child Care' was the second best-selling book of the 20th century. Told parents to trust their instincts — a revolutionary idea at the time.

name: Maryam Mirzakhani
known_for: First woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal, for work on the geometry of surfaces. Died of breast cancer at 40, a devastating loss.

name: Thomas Henry Huxley
known_for: Darwin's self-appointed 'Bulldog,' he championed evolution in public debates with such ferocity that he essentially won the battle Darwin was too shy to fight.

name: Soren Kierkegaard
known_for: The father of existentialism, who wrote under a dozen pseudonyms and argued that truth is subjective — the most influential philosopher you've probably never read in the original.

name: Sigmund Freud
known_for: Whether genius or fraud, he invented the idea of the unconscious mind — and changed how the entire Western world thinks about itself.

name: Pyotr Kapitsa
known_for: Discovered superfluidity in liquid helium and survived refusing to work on the Soviet bomb — one of the few scientists who told Stalin no and lived.

name: Richard Feynman
known_for: Reinvented quantum electrodynamics, cracked safes at Los Alamos for fun, played bongo drums, and explained physics with such joy that he made the universe feel like a playground.

name: Edsger Dijkstra
known_for: Invented the shortest-path algorithm and structured programming. Wrote 1,300+ technical notes by hand and famously declared 'goto' statements harmful.

name: Dorothy Hodgkin
known_for: Used X-ray crystallography to solve penicillin, vitamin B12, and insulin. Won the Nobel while Margaret Thatcher was her student at Oxford.

name: Florence Nightingale
known_for: Pioneered modern nursing AND data visualization. Her 'coxcomb' charts showing preventable military deaths changed public health policy forever.

name: Ronald Ross
known_for: Proved that mosquitoes transmit malaria — a discovery made in sweltering Indian heat that won the Nobel Prize and has saved millions of lives.

name: Maria Gaetana Agnesi
known_for: First woman to write a mathematics textbook and first appointed to a university math chair. Walked away from academia to spend her life caring for the poor.

name: Edward Jenner
known_for: Noticed milkmaids who caught cowpox never got smallpox, and used that observation to develop the first vaccine — from 'vacca,' Latin for cow.

name: Omar Khayyam
known_for: Solved cubic equations, reformed the Persian calendar to be more accurate than the Gregorian, and wrote the Rubaiyat — beloved poetry in any language.

name: Bertrand Russell
known_for: Tried to ground all math in logic, discovered his own devastating paradox, won the Nobel in Literature, and got arrested for peace activism at age 89.

name: Oliver Heaviside
known_for: Self-taught genius who reformulated Maxwell's equations into their modern form and predicted the ionosphere. Died in poverty, ignored by the establishment.

name: Max Perutz
known_for: Spent 22 years solving hemoglobin's structure by X-ray crystallography — the longest sustained attack on a single problem, rewarded with a Nobel Prize.

name: Mary Anning
known_for: A working-class girl from Lyme Regis who discovered the first ichthyosaur at 12. One of the greatest fossil hunters ever, while male scientists took credit.

name: Andrei Sakharov
known_for: Designed the Soviet hydrogen bomb, then became the USSR's most famous dissident. Won the Nobel Peace Prize; the government wouldn't let him collect it.

name: John Bardeen
known_for: Only person to win two Nobel Prizes in Physics — for the transistor and for superconductivity. So quiet that few outside physics know his name.

name: Rachel Carson
known_for: Wrote 'Silent Spring,' launching the environmental movement. The chemical industry tried to destroy her; she changed the world anyway.

name: John Nash
known_for: His equilibrium theory revolutionized economics. Battled paranoid schizophrenia for decades, then recovered to win both the Nobel and Abel prizes.

name: Milutin Milankovic
known_for: Serbian mathematician who calculated how Earth's orbital variations cause ice ages — dismissed for decades, now central to climate science.

name: Peter Higgs
known_for: Predicted the particle that gives others mass. Waited nearly 50 years for the Large Hadron Collider to confirm it. Wept when it did.

name: Chien-Shiung Wu
known_for: Proved that the universe distinguishes left from right — disproving parity conservation. Her male theorist colleagues won the Nobel; she was excluded.

name: Blaise Pascal
known_for: Built a calculator at 18, founded probability theory, proved atmospheric pressure varies with altitude, then abandoned science for theology after a mystical experience.

name: Justus von Liebig
known_for: Father of organic chemistry who invented the modern teaching laboratory. His work on plant nutrition launched the fertilizer industry that feeds most of the world.

name: Charles Drew
known_for: Pioneered blood banking and plasma storage that saved thousands in WWII. Resigned to protest the military's racist policy of segregating blood by race.

name: David Attenborough
known_for: Has been explaining the natural world to humanity for over seven decades. His voice may be the most widely recognized on Earth.

name: Alan Turing
known_for: Invented the universal computer concept, cracked Enigma and helped win WWII, then was prosecuted for being gay and died at 41. The father of computer science and AI.

name: Virginia Apgar
known_for: Invented the Apgar score — the first test every newborn receives. Its elegant simplicity has saved countless infant lives.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
known_for: Invented the World Wide Web in 1989 and gave it away for free. Could have been the richest person on Earth; chose to keep the web open.

name: George Stephenson
known_for: Illiterate until 18, he taught himself to read and built the world's first public railway. His rail gauge became the global standard.

name: E.O. Wilson
known_for: The world's foremost expert on ants who became a prophet of biodiversity, warning that we are causing the sixth mass extinction.

name: Jacques Cousteau
known_for: Co-invented the aqualung, made the ocean accessible to millions, and spent his life exploring the sea aboard his beloved ship Calypso.

name: James Clerk Maxwell
known_for: Unified electricity, magnetism, and light into four equations. Einstein kept his portrait on the wall: 'the most profound physics since Newton.'

name: Luis Alvarez
known_for: Won a Nobel for particle physics, then proposed an asteroid killed the dinosaurs — scoffed at until the Chicxulub crater was found.

name: Alois Alzheimer
known_for: Identified the disease bearing his name by studying the brain of a single patient, Auguste Deter, finding the plaques and tangles that define the condition.

name: Barbara McClintock
known_for: Discovered 'jumping genes' decades before anyone believed her. Won the Nobel Prize at 81 — alone, unshared.

name: Charles Goodyear
known_for: Accidentally dropped rubber and sulfur on a hot stove and discovered vulcanization — the process that made the modern tire possible.

name: William Thomson (Lord Kelvin)
known_for: Established the absolute temperature scale, laid the first transatlantic cable, and famously declared heavier-than-air flight impossible.

name: Maria Mitchell
known_for: First American woman to discover a comet (earning a gold medal from Denmark's king) and first female astronomy professor in the US.

name: Maria Goeppert Mayer
known_for: Developed the nuclear shell model. Second woman to win the Nobel in Physics, after Marie Curie.

name: Tu Youyou
known_for: Searched ancient Chinese texts for malaria cures, found artemisinin in sweet wormwood, and saved millions of lives — winning the Nobel without a PhD.

name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
known_for: Invented calculus independently of Newton (his notation is the one we use), built mechanical calculators, and dreamed of a universal language of logic.

name: Ignaz Semmelweis
known_for: Discovered handwashing could prevent childbed fever, cutting mortality from 18% to 1%. The medical establishment rejected him. He died in an asylum at 47.

name: Ibn al-Haytham
known_for: Father of modern optics. Proved vision works by light entering the eye, invented the camera obscura, and established experimental science centuries before Bacon.

name: Nettie Stevens
known_for: Discovered that sex is determined by X and Y chromosomes. A male colleague received most of the credit during her lifetime.

name: Lise Meitner
known_for: Provided the theoretical explanation for nuclear fission, but Otto Hahn received the Nobel without her. Einstein called her 'the German Marie Curie.'

name: John Wheeler
known_for: Coined 'black hole' and 'wormhole,' mentored Feynman and dozens of luminaries, and spent his career at the wildest frontiers of physics.

name: Nikola Tesla
known_for: Invented alternating current and the Tesla coil, envisioned wireless energy, and spent his last years feeding pigeons in a New York hotel, claiming to love one.

name: George Washington Carver
known_for: Born into slavery, he pioneered sustainable agriculture, developing hundreds of products from peanuts, sweet potatoes, and soybeans.

name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell
known_for: As a grad student, discovered pulsars. Her supervisor won the Nobel; she was excluded — perhaps the greatest Nobel snub in history.

name: Irmgard Flugge-Lotz
known_for: Pioneer of automatic control theory and first woman appointed full professor of engineering at Stanford.

name: Terence Tao
known_for: Often called the Mozart of math. Won the Fields Medal at 31, working across so many areas that colleagues struggle to keep up.

name: Robert Hooke
known_for: Built microscopes and coined the word 'cell.' Feuded with Newton, who may have ensured that no portrait of Hooke survived.

name: Hendrik Lorentz
known_for: Developed the Lorentz transformations — the mathematical backbone of special relativity. Einstein called him the most brilliant physicist he'd met.

name: Thomas Kuhn
known_for: Wrote 'The Structure of Scientific Revolutions' and gave us 'paradigm shift.' Science doesn't progress smoothly but through upheavals.

name: Gregor Mendel
known_for: An Augustinian friar who spent eight years breeding peas and discovered heredity's laws. Ignored for 35 years, then changed biology forever.

name: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
known_for: At 19, on a ship to England, calculated white dwarf maximum mass. Eddington mocked him publicly; decades later Chandra won the Nobel.

name: Abu Musa Jabir ibn Hayyan
known_for: Known as Geber in Europe, this 8th-century polymath pioneered distillation and crystallization. Many consider him the father of chemistry.

name: Vera Rubin
known_for: Found the first compelling evidence for dark matter. Was denied Palomar telescope time because women weren't allowed.

name: Alice Ball
known_for: At 23, developed the most effective leprosy treatment for decades. Died at 24; a male colleague published her work under his name.

name: Rosalind Franklin
known_for: Her Photo 51 was the key to DNA's structure. Watson and Crick used it without acknowledgment. She died at 37, never knowing how central her work was.

name: James Lovelock
known_for: Proposed the Gaia hypothesis and invented the detector that revealed CFCs destroying the ozone layer. Lived to 103.

name: Karl Popper
known_for: Argued that good science is falsifiable — if it can't be proven wrong, it isn't science.

name: Beatrix Potter
known_for: Before Peter Rabbit, she was a serious mycologist whose fungal research was presented to the Linnean Society — by a man, since women couldn't attend.

name: Charles Townes
known_for: Invented the maser and laid groundwork for the laser. The idea came on a park bench; he scribbled it on an envelope.

name: Wangari Maathai
known_for: Founded the Green Belt Movement, planting 51 million trees across Africa. First African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Marie Tharp
known_for: Mapped the ocean floor and discovered the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, proving plate tectonics. Her colleague initially dismissed her finding as 'girl talk.'

name: Tapputi
known_for: A Babylonian perfume-maker from around 1200 BCE — the earliest named chemist in history. Developed distillation millennia before modern chemistry.

name: Archimedes
known_for: Discovered the lever, calculated pi, and leapt from his bath shouting 'Eureka!' His last words to the soldier who killed him: 'Do not disturb my circles.'

name: Euclid
known_for: His 'Elements' — geometry's foundation for 2,000+ years. When a king asked for an easier way: 'There is no royal road to geometry.'

name: Hipparchus
known_for: Created the first star catalog, discovered precession of the equinoxes, and invented trigonometry. The greatest astronomer of antiquity.

name: Zhang Heng
known_for: Invented the first seismoscope, calculated pi accurately, and mapped 2,500 stars in Han Dynasty China.

name: Liu Hui
known_for: Calculated pi to five decimal places with a 3,072-sided polygon and developed proto-calculus 1,300 years before Newton.

name: Hypatia
known_for: The last great scholar of Alexandria, murdered by a mob — one of history's most haunting losses.

name: Zu Chongzhi
known_for: Calculated pi to seven decimal places — a record unbroken for nearly a thousand years.

name: Aryabhata
known_for: Calculated pi to four decimals, proposed Earth rotates on its axis, and contributed foundational ideas about zero.

name: Brahmagupta
known_for: First to treat zero as a number with defined arithmetic rules — including the unsettling problem of dividing by it.

name: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi
known_for: His book gave us 'algebra' and his name gave us 'algorithm.' He created the mathematical language of the modern world.

name: Avicenna (Ibn Sina)
known_for: His 'Canon of Medicine' was the standard textbook for 500 years. Memorized the Quran by 10, practicing medicine by 18.

name: Huang Daopo
known_for: Revolutionized cotton spinning and weaving in 13th-century China, improving millions of lives.

name: Wang Zhenyi
known_for: 18th-century Chinese astronomer who built models to explain eclipses and argued women deserved equal education. Died at 29.

name: Sau Lan Wu
known_for: Key roles in discovering the J/psi particle, gluon, and Higgs boson. One of the most accomplished experimentalists alive.

name: Niels Henrik Abel
known_for: Proved there's no general solution for quintic equations — shattering elegance. Died of tuberculosis at 26, in poverty.

name: Alexander Fleming
known_for: Discovered penicillin by noticing mold killed bacteria in a dish he forgot to clean. That sloppiness saved more lives than any other act in history.

name: Paul Dirac
known_for: Predicted antimatter from pure math. So legendarily silent that colleagues invented a unit — one 'dirac' equals one word per hour.

name: Roger Penrose
known_for: Proved black hole singularities are inevitable, discovered Penrose tiling, and won the Nobel at 89.

name: Amedeo Avogadro
known_for: His hypothesis about equal gas volumes was ignored for 50 years. The impossibly large number named after him is chemistry's bedrock constant.

name: Erwin Chargaff
known_for: Discovered DNA base pairing rules — A pairs with T, C with G — the clue Watson and Crick needed, while Chargaff fumed at being overlooked.

name: Ernest Everett Just
known_for: Pioneering Black biologist whose cell fertilization work was decades ahead. Faced relentless racism and moved to Europe to research in peace.

name: Hans Christian Oersted
known_for: Noticed a compass needle deflect during a lecture — an accidental observation that launched the electromagnetic revolution.

name: Rhazes (al-Razi)
known_for: First to distinguish smallpox from measles systematically. His medical encyclopedia was used for centuries across the Islamic world and Europe.

name: Margaret Hamilton
known_for: Led the Apollo 11 guidance software team. Her error handling prevented a lunar landing abort. Coined 'software engineering.'

name: Orville Wright
known_for: Piloted the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk — 12 seconds, 120 feet, and the beginning of the age of aviation.

name: Katherine Johnson
known_for: Calculated NASA trajectories by hand. John Glenn refused to fly until she personally verified the computer's numbers.

name: Flossie Wong-Staal
known_for: First to clone HIV and map its genes, enabling HIV blood tests. Named top woman scientist of the 1980s.

name: Ernest Rutherford
known_for: Discovered the nucleus by shooting at gold foil — 'as if a cannon shell bounced off tissue paper.' Split the atom and named the proton.

name: Hermann von Helmholtz
known_for: Invented the ophthalmoscope, formulated energy conservation, and mastered acoustics, optics, and thermodynamics.

name: Al-Biruni
known_for: Calculated Earth's circumference to within 1% using a mountain and trigonometry. Wrote encyclopedically on India, astronomy, and pharmacology.

name: August Kekule
known_for: Dreamt of a snake eating its own tail and realized benzene must be a ring — one of chemistry's most famous eureka moments.

name: Aldo Leopold
known_for: Author of 'A Sand County Almanac,' the book that shaped American conservation. We are citizens of the land community, not conquerors.

name: Irene Joliot-Curie
known_for: Daughter of Marie Curie, she carried on the tradition by discovering artificial radioactivity with her husband, winning their own Nobel.

name: Alexander von Humboldt
known_for: Explored South America for five years and essentially invented ecology. More places are named after him than any other person.

name: Dorothy Vaughan
known_for: NASA's first Black supervisor who taught herself FORTRAN when she saw computers replacing humans — adapting before anyone asked.

name: Michael Faraday
known_for: A bookbinder's apprentice who discovered electromagnetic induction, invented the electric motor, and built the foundation of the electrical age.

name: Chen-Ning Yang
known_for: With T.D. Lee, predicted nature doesn't conserve parity. Won the Nobel at 35, first Chinese-born laureate in physics.

name: Asima Chatterjee
known_for: First Indian woman to earn a science doctorate. Developed drugs from indigenous plants for epilepsy and malaria.

name: Svante Arrhenius
known_for: First to calculate that doubling CO2 raises global temperature — in 1896. His PhD thesis barely passed.

name: Enrico Fermi
known_for: Built the first nuclear reactor under a squash court. So rare to master both theory and experiment that they called him 'the Pope.'

name: Meghnad Saha
known_for: His equation explains stellar ionization, making star classification a science instead of guesswork.

name: Niels Bohr
known_for: Built the quantum atom model and smuggled Denmark's Nobel gold past the Nazis by dissolving it in acid.

name: Mildred Dresselhaus
known_for: The 'Queen of Carbon Science' — her work on graphite, fullerenes, and nanotubes laid the foundation for nanotechnology.

name: Rudolf Virchow
known_for: Father of pathology: all cells come from cells. Also a reformer who said epidemics are 'warnings that society is in danger.'

name: Mae Jemison
known_for: First African American woman in space — also a physician, Peace Corps doctor, and dancer.

name: James Chadwick
known_for: Discovered the neutron in 1932, completing the atomic picture and making fission possible.

name: Evariste Galois
known_for: Invented group theory as a teenager, wrote it all down the night before a duel, and was killed at 20. His notes changed algebra forever.

name: Jonas Salk
known_for: Developed the polio vaccine and refused to patent it: 'Could you patent the sun?'

name: Dmitri Ivanovsky
known_for: Discovered viruses in 1892 by proving that tobacco mosaic's agent was too small to be a bacterium.

name: Homi Bhabha
known_for: Father of India's nuclear program and TIFR founder. A cosmic ray physicist who also painted and loved music.

name: Alfred Wegener
known_for: Proposed continental drift. Mocked for decades, he died on a Greenland expedition before plate tectonics proved him right.

name: Janaki Ammal
known_for: Created sugarcane hybrids that made India self-sufficient, then fought to preserve its rainforests.

name: Marie Curie
known_for: First woman to win a Nobel, first person with two in different sciences. Her notebooks are still too radioactive to handle.

name: Konrad Lorenz
known_for: Discovered imprinting by getting goslings to follow him like he was their mother.

name: C.V. Raman
known_for: Discovered the Raman effect — light changing wavelength when scattered — winning India's first science Nobel with cheap equipment.

name: Benjamin Banneker
known_for: Free Black American who taught himself astronomy, published almanacs, and challenged Thomas Jefferson's views on race.

name: Birbal Sahni
known_for: Pioneer who discovered fossils that rewrote ancient Indian flora and founded the Birbal Sahni Institute.

name: Benoit Mandelbrot
known_for: Discovered fractals — infinite patterns repeating at every scale, from coastlines to blood vessels. Proved roughness has its own order.

name: Nikolai Vavilov
known_for: Collected seeds worldwide to protect crop diversity. Lysenko had him arrested. A plant scientist who starved to death in a Soviet prison.

name: Nils Gustaf Dalen
known_for: Won the Nobel for his automatic lighthouse valve. Was blind by the time he received it.

name: Jagadish Chandra Bose
known_for: Demonstrated wireless before Marconi, proved plants feel, and refused to patent anything — science belongs to everyone.

name: Werner Heisenberg
known_for: Invented the uncertainty principle — you can't know both position and momentum, not from bad instruments but because reality is built that way.

name: Grace Hopper
known_for: Invented the first compiler, popularized high-level programming languages, and found the actual moth that coined 'debugging.'

name: Ada Lovelace
known_for: Wrote the first computer program in 1843 for a machine not yet built. Anticipated general-purpose computing a century early.

name: Annie Jump Cannon
known_for: Classified 350,000+ stars by hand, creating the spectral system still used today. Nearly deaf, working by sight alone.

name: Max Born
known_for: Gave quantum mechanics its probabilistic meaning. His granddaughter Olivia Newton-John became a pop star.

name: Robert Koch
known_for: Found the bacteria behind tuberculosis, cholera, and anthrax, and established the rules for proving which germ causes which disease.

name: Tycho Brahe
known_for: Prosthetic nose from a duel, pet moose that died drunk on stairs, and the most precise pre-telescope star observations ever made.

name: Freeman Dyson
known_for: Unified quantum electrodynamics, proposed the Dyson sphere, and remained a brilliant contrarian until 96.

name: Mary Cartwright
known_for: Discovered mathematical chaos decades before chaos theory existed. First woman elected FRS for mathematics.

name: Esther Lederberg
known_for: Discovered lambda phage and invented replica plating. Her husband got the Nobel for work that depended on her innovations.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
known_for: Self-taught Indian clerk who sent astonishing theorems to Cambridge. Died at 32; his notebooks still yield discoveries a century later.

name: James Prescott Joule
known_for: Proved heat is energy, not substance, establishing the first law of thermodynamics. The joule bears his name.

name: Charles Babbage
known_for: Designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s — a mechanical computer never built, but containing every element of modern computing.

name: Mary Somerville
known_for: Self-taught polymath. The word 'scientist' was coined to describe her, since 'man of science' didn't fit.

name: Johannes Kepler
known_for: Discovered planets move in ellipses — shattering 2,000 years of circular dogma — while defending his mother against witchcraft charges.

name: Louis Pasteur
known_for: Disproved spontaneous generation, invented pasteurization, and developed vaccines for anthrax and rabies. The most consequential biologist of the 19th century.

name: Charles Messier
known_for: A comet hunter famous for cataloging 110 'annoying' non-comet objects — nebulae and galaxies now beloved by amateur astronomers.
